Then, indeed, while this Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī was being spoken by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, this entire Sahā world-system became suffused with a magnificent radiance.

And those hundreds of millions of lords of desire who exercise the power of Māra within the hundreds of millions of four-continent worlds in this buddha-field, agitated by the majesty of the Buddha, surveyed these four-continent worlds.
"From where has this radiance arisen?
Surely it is the power of that one called Māra the Evil who dwells there in the world-system of four continents—he who is more powerful, more sovereign, and more majestic than we.
Then those Māras, looking about, beheld that Māra the Evil sitting in his treasury, extremely dejected.
Then those one hundred million Māras went toward this world-system of four continents, to where the abode of the wicked Māra was;
having arrived, they spoke thus to the wicked Māra:
"What is it, O Lord of Desire?"
This entire world-system was illuminated, yet you remained seated, having entered your chamber of grief.
Then Māra, the Lord of Desire, announced in detail to those hundreds of millions of Māras:
"O worthy ones, you should know that a certain ascetic has appeared here from the Śākya clan—one who is exceedingly deceitful and a master of illusion."
As soon as he had arisen, this entire world-system was illuminated, shaken, and agitated.

Whatever wise ones there were here in this entire world-system— whether lords of the great *indrās*, lords of the *nāgas*, lords of the *yakṣas*, lords of the *surendras*, lords of the *mahoragas*, lords of the *garuḍas*, lords of the *kinnaras*, or even other wise humans— they all approached him to perform acts of worship, [having seen] that for six years he sat alone, without a second, manifesting the illusion of the marks [of a Great Man].
He accomplished this.

Desiring likewise to display my own power, I too approached with an entourage of thirty-six koṭis of troops; having surrounded him on all sides, I displayed the entire miraculous power, supernatural might, and prowess of the Māra-forces.
"Behold, I am unable to even cause a single pore of his skin to tremble or inspire fear; how much less could I shake him from that seat, or inflict any other harm?

And yet, such an illusion has been displayed by this low-born man, and such a trembling has been wrought, that I, along with my army, have been defeated and fallen upon the earth like a severed tree."
And while seated right there, he accomplished such a signless illusion by which the entire domain of Māra was overcome. Having mastered that vidyā, he rose from it and revealed it to sentient beings.

"I know the minds of whoever here in this world-system of four continents are wise, discerning, and have formed an aspiration for that illusion, as well as their destiny and rebirth among the six realms of existence.
And as for those who have gone for refuge to it, I am not able to terrify or disturb even a single pore of their skin."
Nor could I, in this world, again cause him to be contradicted or shaken.

And this very day, my five hundred female attendants and twenty thousand sons, together with their retinues and assemblies, have gone for refuge to the low-born ascetic Gautama and are seated before him; I am no longer able to separate them from him.
"Therefore, may you become powerful, meritorious, wise, and influential friends;
we shall deprive that low-born son of the Śākyas of his life,
and we shall destroy all those beings who have gone for refuge to him."
We shall defeat the dark side of the ascetics, characterized by illusion and deceit;
we shall illuminate the bright side of Māra.
Thereafter, we shall dwell in comfort and ease.
Then Māra Jyotiṣprabha surveyed this Jambudvīpa, where the Tathāgata was seated and teaching the Dharma.
Then Māra Jyotiṣprabha beheld the body of the Blessed One and heard his teaching of the Dharma, which was endowed with a melodious voice. At that very moment, a hair-raising terror arose within him.
Then he spoke thus to Māra, the Evil One:
"For in this entire field, he is preeminent, possessing excellent form, merit, and wisdom; he is pure and long-enduring."
Having been liberated from afflictions for a long time and being well-established on the path,
all his existences are exhausted and he is freed from sorrow.
Do not fall again under the sway of anger; this is improper,
for he is the foremost, the most excellent, and the refuge in these three worlds.
He in whom not even a trace of hatred appears toward this [teaching] is deluded and shall be deprived of happiness in this world.
Then another Māra, named Sannimika, spoke thus to that Māra, the Evil One:
"He possesses great supernatural power and is endowed with the marks of excellent merit; indeed, he is independent and liberated from all states of existence.
As the teacher of the path to the complete destruction of suffering, he cannot be harmed by hundreds of Māras."
The Evil One said:
"Bring my people under your control; these people of yours will follow his lead.
Before long he will make our realm empty; where then will our refuge be?"
Then the Māra named Vanarāja said this to the Evil Māra:
"When you possessed supreme prosperity, you displayed your own prowess;
now, defeated by his power and devoid of hope, why do you still compete with the Omniscient One today?"
Khaḍgasoma Māra said:
"In some respects he has no malice of mind, nor does he remain impure in his mental disposition."
Having attained a state of movement liberated from the three realms, he indeed cannot be slain by others.
The Evil One said:
"Those who are seated here in this world-system, attached to sensual desires and intoxicated by pride and delusion—
since they are my servants and always follow my will, how could it not be possible for them all together to cause his destruction?"
The Māra named Kṣititoya spoke thus:
"Having fully understood that all phenomena are essence-less, like illusions and mirages, he has subdued his thirst;
unattached to states of existence and having the nature of space—how could it be possible to cause him any hindrance?"
The Evil One said:
"Right here in this triple world, he has mastery over one who enjoys delicious food, drink, seats, and clothing."
And since the three types of sensation are established within his mind, how indeed could it be possible to bring them to an end?
The Māra named Tṛṣṇañjaha spoke thus:

"Whatever supernatural power exists in this realm belonging to the Evil Ones and even to the great serpents, it does not touch even a fraction of Siddhārtha’s power; for how could it possibly bring about his destruction?"
The Evil One said:
"Indeed, I have caused his food to be cut off, and that rock was thrown [at him] again;
likewise, cries of 'Alas! were uttered from the hermitage, and he was even shaken."
The Māra named Bodhākṣa spoke thus:
"When you caused him some obstruction, was he provoked by that to show anger,
or did he display a frown on his face, or did you hear harsh words from him in person?"
The Evil One said:
"He always proceeds with discernment; he has abandoned passion and is free from hatred and delusion."
He possesses a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, and his conduct in social interaction is likewise constant.
The Māra named Durdharṣa spoke thus:
"We shall strive for the destruction of those who are bound by the snares of the three fetters;
but how indeed can he, whose snares of affliction and delusion have been abandoned, be led to destruction?"
The Evil One said:
"Now that you have attained power, become my immediate allies; remain vigilant!
I shall command the waters, the entire earth, and all the directions garlanded with mountains."
From the sky, I shall unleash a fierce rain of clouds and mountains, and heaps of iron filings;
I shall hurl iron arrows, spears, razors, and javelins at his body for the purpose of pulverizing it.
By these applications, blazing with blows, I shall reduce that Lion of the Śākyas to ashes.
And so on, until ten million Māras had spoken ten million verses.
Then all the Māras spoke with one voice:
"So be it."
"We shall depart from our respective abodes;
having donned our armor, we will come with our armies and retinues and display the full extent of our supernatural power and domain.
Then you yourself will know what kind of heroism that ascetic Gautama displays at that moment."
Then those tens of millions of Māras went to their own abodes, put on their armor, and— each accompanied by a retinue of ten million Māras,
donning various types of mail and equipped with diverse weapons and arrayed in various defensive gear— arrived in this Jambudvīpa at the end of that very night.

At the border of Aṅga and Magadha, all those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, and kumbhāṇḍas who were situated in the sky throughout this world-system of four continents— those whose minds were not serene toward the Blessed One, who had not attained a respectful attitude, and whose minds were not serene toward the Dharma and the Saṅgha—
all of them were incited by Māra, the Evil One, to kill the Blessed One.

They too, clad in various armor and bearing weapons, stood right there. Māra, the Evil One, having gone to the side of the Himalayas where the seer Jyotīrasa dwelt— one who was a devotee of Maheśvara, had reached the perfection of the eighteen branches of knowledge and the sphere of supernatural powers, and was accompanied by a retinue of five hundred— stood before him in the form of Maheśvara and spoke as follows.
It is certain that the eminent seer born of the Gautama clan, renowned and relying upon the superknowledges, dwells here in Magadha; today he is wandering for alms at the king’s palace.
Remain steadfast and converse with him clearly on various topics of discourse.
Right there, you too shall certainly attain the five supernormal powers and mastery.
Then Māra the Evil One, having spoken this verse, vanished right there;
having gone to his own abode, he announced to the Māras in his assembly:
"O friends, listen today to the kind of incomparable wisdom that has been conceived by me."
Speak freely with the Son of the Śākyas, who is endowed with the power of supernatural faculties;
do not display that illusion belonging to your own realm. Māra’s pride is great, yet he is always gentle in speech, restrained toward his disciples like a mother toward her sons.
For those disciples of his who have abandoned negligence surely wander about in the city during the forenoon, moving steadily and quietly at their own leisure; meanwhile, we two—
(Dutt 60)
Let us quickly seize him with the essential elements of sweet dancing and song, so that upon hearing this display, that bull among the Śākyas may fall into a state of mental despondency.
Another Māra spoke thus:
"Let lions, tigers, elephants, camels, and fierce buffaloes, many in number and emitting harsh cries like the thundering of monsoon clouds, be swiftly conjured outside this city."
"Armed with weapons and missiles, we shall stand here; seeing us directly, he will be bewildered by these wonders, abandon his supernatural power, and then depart, forgetting the various directions."
Another Māra said:
"Standing repeatedly at street corners, crossroads, and gateways with hideous faces,
and brandishing various weapons such as sharp lances, arrows, spears, darts, swords, and scimitars."
From the sky, releasing thunderbolts from clouds with loud roars as their excellent weapons,
he will quickly fall under the power of that earthquake out of fear.
In detail, they all described exactly how those Māras were manifesting their power and domain;
and the Blessed One, moreover, established this entire great trichiliocosm as consisting of adamant.
Furthermore, the Māras no longer raised a clamor, nor did mountains of fire remain in the four directions.
There were no black clouds, no unseasonable winds, and not a single nāga poured down even a single drop of rain, through the empowerment of the Buddha’s power.
Furthermore, at that time, four great śrāvakas, having dressed in the forenoon and taken their bowls and robes, entered the great city of Rājagṛha for alms.
The Venerable Śāriputra entered the great city of Rājagṛha through the southern city gate for alms.
In that city, fifty Māra youths—possessing supreme youth and beauty, and appearing like great beings—were wandering about dancing and singing.
They seized the Venerable Śāriputra with both hands and ran through the street, dancing and singing, and said this to Śāriputra:
"Dance, O śramaṇa! Sing, O śramaṇa!
Śāriputra said, "Listen to me yourselves, sirs!"
"I shall cause you to hear a song never heard before.
And all those Māra-kumāras, running along with Śāriputra to the sound of the song, said this:
"Enough indeed with these sense-bases; we have been deceived by these sense-bases!"
For these sense-bases are places of slaughter; I shall bring an end to these sense-bases.
Enough indeed with these things fashioned from the aggregates; we have been deceived by these things fashioned from the aggregates.
For the aggregates fashioned from the aggregates are like execution grounds; I shall bring an end to these things fashioned from the aggregates.
Namely: vaha-ra vaha-ra / bhāra-vaha marīci-vaha / satya-vaha ama-vaha / svāhā //
The Elder Śāriputra, running along, spoke these verses and these mantra-words in a singing voice.
Then those fifty Māra youths, exceedingly thrilled and with minds full of serene faith, said this:
"We now ask forgiveness from you, our Lord, the kinsman and the true guide of the world."
Just as those aggregates have been declared by you to be fraught with danger, we are your constant witnesses regarding them.
And they all, having bowed their heads at the feet of Śāriputra in the middle of the street, sat down before him to hear the Dharma.
Then, indeed, the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana entered the great city of Rājagṛha for alms through the eastern city gate;
yet even there, the fifty Māra youths spoke in the very same melodic song.
Enough indeed with these things made of elements; we have been robbed by those things made of elements.

they shake off the four kinds of Māras, just as this Lion of the Śākyas does now.

Then, when Māra saw all those Māras along with their retinues having gone for refuge to the ascetic Gautama, he became even more agitated, terrified, and bewildered, and weeping, he spoke thus:

"I shall cut the root of the lotus by which beings depart in all directions;

Having reflected thus, Māra the Evil One descended from the sky like the wind; proceeding toward where that lotus lay upon the path, he attempted to uproot it by its stalk, yet he was not even able to touch it.
When he wished to sever its petals, he could not see them at all.
He even desired to strike the pericarp of the lotus with his hand, yet he could not reach it at all;
just as lightning is seen but not apprehended,
or just as a shadow is seen but not apprehended.

In this very way, that lotus was seen but could not be grasped. And when Māra the Evil One saw that lotus, yet could neither grasp it nor touch it, he then desired to let out a loud, most terrifying cry in order to terrify the entire assembly;
even that he was unable to do.
Furthermore, with great force and speed, he desired to strike and shake the great earth with both hands; yet he was unable even to touch it, nor did he perceive it at all.
It was just as if someone were to desire to grasp the sky, but could not perceive it.
In this very way, Māra the Evil One saw the earth, yet he could neither touch it nor grasp it. This thought occurred to him:
"What if I were to strike a blow at these beings who have gathered here, or cause a distraction of their minds?"
He saw those beings, yet he did not perceive even a single being, nor did he touch them;
then Māra the Evil One wept all the more intensely,
and through the Buddha’s majestic power, his entire body trembled like a tree.
With tears on his face, looking toward the four directions, he spoke thus:
"This is an illusion created by the ascetic for the sake of winning over the entire world today,
by which I have been deluded before my eyes and have fallen into this confusion in an instant."
I have fallen from my realm due to the exhaustion of my own merit, and my life is spent;
I am quickly departing, rejected, before I go to my destruction and reach my own abode.
He desired to go even to his own abode, but he was unable to go there either;
becoming even more terrified, he wept,
and this thought arose within him:

"I am exhausted by my supernatural power; let me not fall under the control of this ascetic, nor let my life come to an end in the presence of this enemy. Nevertheless, he was unable to vanish or flee in any direction; there, he saw himself bound at the neck with fivefold bonds.
Becoming even more enraged and terrified, he cried out loudly and said:
"Alas, my dear son and kinsmen! I shall never see you again!"
Then a Māra named Ghoṣavati, having assumed the form of a seated universal monarch, spoke thus to the Evil Māra:
"O sir, why are you today so sorrowful in mind, weeping with a distorted face and voice?
Go quickly, without fear, for refuge to the Best of Sages, the Supreme One in all the world, who is worthy of protection."
He is the protection, the refuge of the world, the lamp, the shelter, and the lord who removes the three types of suffering;
yet if you do not attend upon him, you will not attain the bliss of peace and happiness.
Then it occurred to Māra, the Evil One:
"What if I were to go for refuge to the ascetic Gautama with words of satisfaction, so that I might be released from these bonds?
Then Māra, the Evil One, bowed with palms joined toward the direction in which the Blessed One was staying and spoke thus:
Homage to that supreme person, the liberator from old age and disease!
Thus do I go for refuge to that Buddha, the Blessed One. And he said:
"O Protector, quickly [deliver me] from this great and most perilous fear, from the bondage of the Sage."
May I be released; from this day forward, I have come for refuge to the Sugata, the Foremost One.
Blinded by delusion and filled with rage, I previously committed a great offense against you.
I confess all of that before you, having established you as my witness.
And when Māra the Evil One had gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Blessed One, with words of satisfaction, he perceived himself as liberated.
But when it occurred to him, "I shall depart from this assembly," he again perceived himself bound at the neck with fivefold bonds.
When he was no longer able to go anywhere, he then generated a mind of seeking protection and refuge in the presence of the Blessed One.
While sitting right there, he perceived himself as being released again, up to perceiving himself as bound and released seven times.
Thus ends the third chapter, "The Subduing of Māra," in the *Mahāsannipāta-ratnaketu-sūtra*. // 3 //

Then the Blessed One set out from the courtyard of the monastery.
There was a tree deity there named Dyutindharā; weeping most piteously, she bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One and spoke thus:
"O Protector, now the entire triple world will be deprived of its sight."
Now that you have gone to your destruction, while the sage Sarvārthasiddha has his every wish fulfilled,
these serpents with tongues like whips, armed with sharp swords and arrows and possessing mouths of fire, roam this sky seeking your ruin; do not go there now!

And when the Blessed One descended into the gateway chamber, then the deity of the gateway chamber named Jyotivaraṇā, weeping with a loud voice, bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One and spoke thus:
"In this supreme city, there are twenty thousand who are known as brahmins."
With flaming mouths and weapons of sharp blades and arrows, those merciless ones gaze upon one another; twenty thousand of them, possessing such extreme ferocity and cruelty,
stand here for your destruction— so do not go, O pure-faced one!
Then the Blessed One entered the gate-hall.
There, a deity named Tamālasārā, the guardian of the city of Rājagṛha,
approached the Blessed One in haste, weeping with a loud voice.
Having approached and bowed his head at [the Buddha's] feet, he spoke thus:
"O Blessed One, this path is once again surrounded by lions, camels, and rutting elephants;
and for the sake of harassing the monks, Māras have created many obstacles."

O you whose voice is like the sound of clouds, other wanderers of rival sects are intent upon slaying you, the Teacher, on this earth; through the compassion of gods and nāgas, do not go forth, O one of blazing radiance!
Having seen that the destruction of your teaching has been carried out, the lords of men, gods, serpents, and kinnaras have gathered together;
terrified, O Blessed One, vanquisher of Māra, they flee from the Māras.
And furthermore, those whose faces were extremely distorted, being shrouded by illusion.
There will be a great destruction of the True Dharma and a calamity for the world;
the sky will have the luster of the stars extinguished, and there will be a confusion of the moon and the sun.
Alas, observing that the virtuous man has now become tasteless and his head is being struck loudly, he cries out "Woe! What misery!", fearing the loss of his own state.
This world, whose sun has set, perishes; the torch of Dharma goes to its destruction.
Death devours the Fully Awakened One, and the water of Dharma dries up.
When the destruction of those who practice the true Dharma is imminent in the world,
it is precisely from this that the manifestation of non-existent Māras occurs.
Then that deity, not seeing the Blessed One turn back, her face bathed in tears, spoke thus:
"O Sage, look upon the entire world; O best of speakers, do not go to your destruction today! If you meet your end in my city, I shall forever be censured by the three worlds."
Listen to my words, O Leader, Essence of Beings: do not go to your destruction in my city today!
Out of compassion for beings, wait here and liberate them from the fear and suffering of birth.
Remember your former vow, O Tathāgata: "Having attained the supreme [enlightenment], may I become a savior.
O best among living beings, bring comfort to the many sentient beings tormented by manifold sufferings!
O you who abide as the supreme form for many millions of eons, alas, the multitude of fools is attached to sensual desires;
therefore, for their pacification, teach the path of Dharma, which consists of the sense bases, faculties, and objects that are empty of intrinsic nature.

Then the Blessed One descended into the gate-hall. At that very moment, the earth goddess named Dṛḍhā, together with ten thousand deities of great power and majesty, stood before the Blessed One with her face bathed in tears and her hair disheveled, with palms joined in reverence, and spoke thus:

Remember your primary purpose: that you have offered the four oceans filled with blood, as well as your heads, bones, the Cakravāḍa mountains, and eyes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. (Rkp 4.21)
In this way, there were various kinds of jewels in the past, as well as sons, wives, elephants, and horses;
dwellings, clothing, bedding, food, drink, and likewise the desired medicines for the sick.
Supreme worship has been performed for the Self-Existent Ones by you, and ethical discipline has been guarded by you without negligence;
patience and learning have indeed been cultivated constantly, as well as reverence toward mother and father.
Innumerable difficult deeds have been accomplished, and beings have indeed been liberated from manifold calamities;
for you made this vow in the beginning of old: "May I become a Buddha, a teacher of the ultimate truth."
May I ferry the multitude across the great flood; may I indeed teach the Dharma to the world;
and may I dry up the roots of craving, the great fears, and all sufferings without exception.

I shall cause the multitude of beings to enter the city of fearlessness; having established them upon the path to supreme enlightenment, I shall liberate those afflicted by manifold sufferings and bring that realm of beings to fulfillment.
O Lord, forgive those here who are addicted to the path of evil conduct and who destroy their learning and virtue;
fulfill this vow and promise of yours, and teach the Dharma for many tens of millions of eons.
O Protector, deliver the world from the flood and bathe it with the water of the eightfold path;
for there are no beings in the three worlds equal to you, O Protector, indeed, there is none more excellent than you.
Being yourself liberated, liberate this world as well; rescue the universe from the ocean of the three realms of existence.
You are the sole kinsman, the unique friend of the world; remain forever and distribute the Dharma.
Then the Blessed One descended into the gate-hall.
At that very moment, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, moving through the sky with tearful faces, spoke thus:
"In the past, we indeed beheld the Sugatas at a time of peace, when their disciples were well-disciplined."
For those who were giving extensive instruction in the Dharma, no such obstacle as this ever occurred.
For this Teacher, of noble intellect, having attained self-becomehood in an exceedingly degenerate age,
the Lord of Munis taught the Dharma concerning the afflictions and so forth in the world for the sake of maturing all beings.
Moreover, O Lion of Speakers, stay here! Many thousands of millions of evil ones are thus destroying the Dharma; do not enter the city today, O Heroic Buddha.
Then another deity spoke thus:
"The wheel was set in motion in a single region by those former Victors who were devoted to the welfare of the world;
let this one, however, go wherever it may, lest it meet with its end today."
Then another deity also spoke thus:
"O Caravan Leader, out of compassion you have wandered here performing exceedingly great benefit for sentient beings;
my thought is only this: let him not meet with destruction in this city today."
Then, at that time, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, with tearful and sorrowful faces,
descended from the path of the sky and stood before the Blessed One, performing various kinds of self-mortification; some tore out their hair.
Some cast off their ornaments;
some caused their parasols, banners, and flags to fall;
and some prostrated themselves upon the ground with their entire bodies.
Some grasped the feet of the Blessed One;
some wept most bitterly;
some beat their breasts with their hands.
Some, standing at the feet of the Blessed One, turned around like waterfowl;
some, standing before the Blessed One with palms joined in reverence, offered praises and prostrations;
and some scattered flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, garments, ornaments, golden threads, pearl necklaces, and blossoms over the Blessed One.
Then many other tens of millions of deities spoke thus with one voice and in loud tones:
"Indeed, for the sake of the world, you have performed many exceedingly difficult austerities.
You have appeared here now in this time when [the Dharma] was exhausted; remain as one who is equanimous and do not abandon us!"
"O blameless one, the work of a Buddha has been accomplished by you only slightly, and very few gods and humans have been made witnesses.
Remain and illuminate the Dharmas for a very long time; deliver the world from this ocean of the three realms of existence."
For there are many beings who perform virtuous deeds, whose seeds are fully ripened, and who are vessels for the nectar of immortality; therefore,
O Lord of the World, manifest compassion for these people and deliver them from the floods.
To those who wander here in the midst of the forest, their path lost in the wilderness of saṃsāra,
show them their own way and deliver them through the words of the noble, supreme Dharma.
This turning of the excellent wheel of Dharma, which is most wonderful and marvelous through its compassion, is even more marvelous for you.
O you of noble intellect, may you remain for a long time; let the people not indeed be without a protector.
Then another deity spoke thus:
"If Vināyaka goes to his destruction, then the entire world will become blind;
for the sake of the three liberations, the Eightfold Path will here cease to exist in every respect."
We have sown this auspicious seed in you with our bodies and minds, being diligent for the sake of your upliftment;
therefore, may we be endowed with all happiness, and may there never be an exhaustion of this mine of merit.
At that time, many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of Śuddhāvāsa deities had also assembled right there;
they too spoke as follows:
"Do not fear; no adverse state shall befall this sage of noble intellect.
We ourselves have previously witnessed what happened when tens of millions of Māras descended upon this holy man on earth."
The terrifying army of Māra, extending thirty-six *yojanas* in every direction with its swift and impetuous advance, filled with the harsh clamor of many spears, swords,
and broad blades, arrived at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*) and instantly dissolved in fear.
Why would that [obstacle] now cause an impediment for one who has attained his goal and whose fame has spread?
Then another deity, weeping, spoke thus:
"In the past, Māra had but a single army, yet it was not of great power;
this army of thousands of millions of Māras is truly of great power."
Without a doubt, the Guide of the World has met his destruction here;
through his passing, this world will wander in darkness, deprived of light.
Then indeed, those Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors, having circumambulated the feet of the Blessed One, spoke thus:
"Please remain here; we pray you, O Foremost of the Compassionate, act for the sake of those of dull intellect.
Many tens of millions of gods are tormented by great sorrow; now, sprinkle them with the essence of the Dharma."

(Dutt 95) Then the Blessed One, having gazed upon that entire assembly with his wide eyes of loving-kindness, spoke thus in a Brahma-like voice, consoling them: "Do not fear; be free from fear today! All the Māras, together with their hosts and their vehicles, [shall be powerless]."
All of them together are not able to frighten even a single hair of mine, let alone my entire body.
Today I shall comfort all the world; I will always teach the Dharma upon this earth.
To those who have strayed from the path, I alone shall provide a clear and perfect instruction on the way.
In the past, I performed many difficult deeds; I gave away abundant food and drink, as well as no small amount of dwellings and medicines. Who is able to cause me hindrance today?
Indeed, I have renounced horses, chariots, and elephants, as well as ornaments and finery;
I have given up male and female slaves, towns, and kingdoms—who then is capable of obstructing me?
Wife, sons, daughters, the circle of my kin, desired sovereignty, and a royal lineage on earth—
all these have been given by me for the benefit of sentient beings; why then should the destruction of my body occur today?
Even if my head, both eyes, ears, nose, hands, feet, skin, flesh, and blood,
as well as my very life, were to be surrendered here by embodied beings, who would be capable of inflicting violence upon me?
Indeed, many tens of millions of Buddhas have been worshipped by me with great devotion and with my own hands;
yet, though I am constantly devoted to ethical discipline, learning, and patience, my mind is not capable of committing a transgression.
In the past, indeed, many difficult deeds were performed by me with extreme composure;
even when my limbs were severed, my mind was not provoked to anger. Who is capable today of inflicting harm upon me?
The afflictions have been conquered by me; I am the Buddha, established in self-mastery, and my mind is filled with loving-kindness toward all sentient beings.
I have no envy, no stubbornness, and no anger; today, no one at all is capable of standing before me.
I have conquered the entire host of Māra; many tens of millions of Māras have been defeated by me.
I shall certainly effect your liberation; do not fear. Why then should I not enter the city?
Whatever Buddhas there are here in the ten directions who remain for the sake of sentient beings,
I shall bring all those Buddhas and the Bodhisattvas of great supernatural power together here.
I shall completely fill the entire field and cause it to be inhabited by means of wisdom and merit;
established as a leader together with those very Buddhas, I shall perform the deeds approved by the Buddhas.
Then, at that time, immeasurable and incalculable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans,
and non-humans gave their applause to the Blessed One and spoke thus:
Homage to the one endowed with marvelous, wondrous, and incalculable vigor! Homage, homage to the Buddha, the Blessed One, who is endowed with the most marvelous qualities!

By the Blessed One, the world including the gods has been comforted; by the Blessed One, the faction of Māra has been defeated; and the turbidity of the afflictions that bind sentient beings has been shaken off.
The mountain of pride among sentient beings has been abandoned;
the tree of birth has been cut down;
it has been pulverized.
The sun of death has been dispelled; the darkness of ignorance has been shaken off; and those of other sects have been brought to clarity.
The four floods have been dried up;
the torches of the Dharma have been kindled;
the path to awakening has been shown.
He was established in patience and gentleness;
he was made to sport in the bliss of meditative concentration;
and the four noble truths were brought to his realization.
The world, together with its gods, has been delivered from the ocean of birth by the Blessed One, the Teacher of great compassion;
sentient beings have been led into the city of fearlessness.
Then those gods and humans, having honored the Blessed One with various flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ornaments, and decorations, beautified the road for the sake of the Blessed One.
They covered the Blessed One with divine garments, flowers, and cloths.

They also covered him with divine *māndārava*, *mahāmāndārava*, *pārūṣaka*, *mahāpārūṣaka*, *mañjūṣaka*, *roca*, *mahāroca*, blue lotuses, white water lilies, and white lotuses. Wherever the Blessed One set down his two feet, on that path they manifested divine trees made of the seven precious gems on both sides and adorned them with divine garments, cloths, and ornaments for the hands, ears, and heads.
And among those trees, they constructed divine lotus ponds,
filled with cool, sweet, clear, and limpid water endowed with the eight qualities, adorned all around with ornaments of the seven precious gems,
and held parasols made of the seven precious gems in the air above.
They rained down banners, flags, golden threads, and pearl necklaces, as well as showers of gold dust;
they released showers of silver and beryl dust, agallochum, tagara, sandalwood, kālānusārin, and tamāla leaves;
and [showers] of gośīrṣa and uragasāra sandalwood dust.
And they rained down upon that path;
with golden threads, pearl necklaces, jewels, and pearls, they adorned the entire expanse of the sky with various celestial ornaments.
Then, outside that city, gods and humans prepared the beauty of the road for the purpose of worshipping the Blessed One.
And within the city, Māra and his retinue displayed magnificent arrays for the purpose of honoring the Blessed One.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One entered the samādhi called Śūraṅgama;
and by means of that samādhi, he proceeded along the road as if he had remained absorbed in it.
Furthermore, at that time, the Blessed One set out upon that path with various kinds of bodily forms, marks, and modes of deportment.
There, those beings who were to be disciplined by Brahmā and had devotion for Brahmā saw the Blessed One walking on the path in the form of Brahmā;

likewise, those who were to be disciplined by Śakra, those to be disciplined by Nārāyaṇa, those to be disciplined by Maheśvara, and those to be disciplined by the Four Great Kings [saw him in their respective forms].

Those who were to be disciplined by a universal monarch (cakravartin), those to be disciplined by a local king (koṭṭarāja), those to be disciplined by a great seer (maharṣi), those to be disciplined by a śramaṇa,

those to be disciplined by Māra, those to be disciplined by a woman, those to be disciplined by a lion, those to be disciplined by an elephant, those to be disciplined by a nāga, and those to be disciplined by an asura; those who were devoted to hares and were to be disciplined by a hare— by means of the form, marks, and deportment of a hare, [they approached] the Blessed One.
They saw him walking along the road.
Those beings who were to be disciplined by a Buddha saw the Blessed One walking along the road with the very form, marks, and deportment of a Buddha.
And all those beings, having joined their palms in reverence, followed closely behind him as they praised and paid homage to him.

Now at that time, the seer named Jyotīrasa, who dwelt in the vicinity of the Himalayas and had been incited by Māra the Evil One, was waiting near the gate of the great city of Rājagṛha with a retinue of five hundred. He beheld the Blessed One’s physical form, marks, and deportment, as well as the innumerable tree deities on the road intent upon performing acts of worship.
Having seen this, the following thought occurred to him:
"This great seer is a speaker of truth, possessed of great majesty, and worthy of worship. ...

[omission] ... Then the seer Jyotīrasa, together with his retinue, beheld the Blessed One endowed with the form, marks, and deportment of a Buddha; as his former roots of merit became manifest, he attained the bodhisattva samādhi called Ratnaketu.
"That concentration which is unshakeable by any meditative attainments"—
then the great seer Jyotīrasa, standing before the Blessed One with palms joined, having offered a flower and offered praise, said:
"The Lord of the World of infinite virtues is truthful and well-established."
All has been spoken by you, whose light is the eye of knowledge for all the world;
your vigor and loving-kindness always arise for the benefit of sentient beings.
Homage to you today, O essence of beings, leader free from attachment!
O you of golden hue, shining like refined gold, your cool rays connect all sentient beings with the qualities that serve as the cause for attaining awakening.
By turning the wheel of Dharma, you have destroyed the mountain of afflictions;
this is the finality of your conduct, the cause of the wisdom of enlightenment.
O Great Physician, Essence of Beings, adorned with the [major] marks, having become a Buddha for the sake of teaching, you have been entreated by the Leader today:
"Cut through my web of views; having crossed over, may I ferry across the world."
After how long will you become a Buddha? Please teach us, O Supreme among Men.
Deliver beings from the ocean of existence, which is a flood of suffering, and establish them on the secure path of Nirvana that is free from outflows;
likewise for all the Buddhas in the ten directions, who are like oceans in their virtues.
To them, who are devoted to the awakening mind, I make this request.
May all the merit of my body, speech, and mind throughout the three times— [which has been touched by the suffering of all beings and is fierce, pure, and harsh]—
thereby cause the minds of all sentient beings to become cooled.
And one shall attain nirvāṇa in the eternally secure buddha-field.
May all sentient beings' diseases and the waters of their afflictions dry up; may they obtain wisdom and faculties that are inherently essential.
And may those sentient beings who are oppressed by the suffering of slaughter and bondage [be liberated].
May they also quickly be liberated through the power of my merit.
May every single being obtain all the qualities of the ocean;
may they satisfy everyone with immeasurable merit, wisdom, and happiness.
May they quickly attain right view, cleansed of all evil; may all these beings become rememberers of their past lives and practitioners of the Dharma.
May they cross to the further shore of the ocean of existence for the sake of accomplishing the Dharma;
and may I also inspire serene faith in the Buddha, who has reached the further shore of all phenomena.
"May you remain for immeasurable eons, raining down the rain of Dharma;
may all sentient beings be bathed by the water from the cloud of Dharma."
Whatever transgression I have committed with body, mind, or speech,
I confess it and entreat the Buddha and the Saṅgha out of reverence for all sentient beings.
And I shall no longer perform actions born of evil views,
having always beheld inconceivable persons standing before me.
Whatever merit I possess, I dedicate that again toward awakening;
for the sake of all beings, I am willing to endure every form of suffering.
May I establish all sentient beings on the supreme path to enlightenment,
and may I traverse the ocean of wisdom throughout the fields for aeons.
Since the touch of awakening is indeed to be attained through purity,
he must surely be established upon the stage of patience toward all sentient beings.
May I attain the five supernormal knowledges in the presence of the Lion of Speakers; having seen the unattached Leader, may you teach the treatise everywhere.
If I shall become a Buddha in the world, the charioteer of all dharmas, let those who stand in the sky cast down canopies of loose flowers; let them remain there.
May they become subject to the will of the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and others;
and may the earth tremble as it bows its head at your feet.
Then the seer Jyotīrasa threw those flowers toward the Blessed One, and they remained suspended above him like a single parasol.
Seeing this, the seer Jyotīrasa, overflowing with an even greater measure of spiritual joy and gladness, prostrated himself at the feet of the Blessed One.
As soon as the seer Jyotīrasa had fallen at the feet of the Blessed One,
at that very moment the trichiliocosm shook in six ways,
and immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of beings there attained minds free from agitation.

Those beings who were to be disciplined by an elephant, upon seeing the Sugata in the form of an elephant, were filled with satisfaction; they scattered flowers over the Great Sage from above, and those flowers remained suspended in the air.
Seeing that earthquake, they were moved even more intensely by wonder and prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One.
Furthermore, those beings who were to be disciplined by a Buddha, all of them, upon seeing the Blessed One’s manifestation as a Buddha, were struck with amazement.
Then the Blessed One arose from the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. Seeing him emerge from that samādhi, those beings who were to be disciplined by a Buddha were filled with extreme joy and gladness;
they scattered over the Blessed One whatever flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, garments, ornaments, and decorations they had obtained, and they spoke these verses:
"Arise quickly and listen; O Great Seer, I shall prophesy for you to attain awakening," so spoke the Leader;
at that moment, the earth trembled with great majesty.
And the flowers became parasols in the sky.
"You are our Buddha, the foremost of bipeds; O All-pervading One, you are the Teacher for the welfare of the world,
possessing infinite merit as vast as space."
The essence of the three worlds, the lamp of the universe.

yet they will demonstrate conditioned phenomena as characterized by arising and passing away.
The Tathāgatas have attained the method of suchness (*tathatā*), which is the differentiation of all forms, syllables, and words.
Sister, the Tathāgata does not contradict suchness; he does so through a single sameness, namely, the sameness of space.
Space, too, is characterized by the absence of superimposition and the cessation of the three formative activities (*saṃskāra*).

Just as space is without conceptualization and without discursive thought regarding conditioned phenomena, even so is the Tathāgata. He does not proliferate, conceptualize, or discriminate regarding the qualities of sensual desire; he does not dwell upon them, nor does he adhere to them.
Likewise, he does not proliferate, adhere to, dwell upon, conceptualize, or discriminate regarding a living soul, a creature, a nourisher, a person, or the aggregates and sense-bases.
"How is it, sister, that you conceptualize the body of the Tathāgata?
The Tathāgata Amitāyus said:
"O Śakra, Lord of the Devas, speak after having reflected."
May you not experience an undesirable result for a long time.
For this is a great true person (*mahāsatpuruṣa*) who has performed services for many Buddhas and has planted roots of merit in the presence of the Blessed Buddhas.
Furthermore, by this true person, a well-adorned female form was manifested for the purpose of making an offering to the Tathāgata.
"Do not treat him with the behavior of a woman.
Then Śakra, bearing the crest-lock, spoke thus to Brahmā, the Lord of Beings:
"Forgive me, noble son, out of compassion for me."
"May I not incur the undesirable fruit of these words.
Then the Bodhisattva Kautūhalika said:
"Blessed One, if Śakra had not confessed this speech, what would have been his [consequence]?"
Regarding the ripening of the fruit,

the Tathāgata Amitāyus said: "If, noble son, this had not been confessed by him, he would have taken upon himself the state of a woman— contemptible as a womb of desire— for eighty-four thousand births."
"Therefore, then, the action of speech must be guarded.
May it be granted to you, noble son, through the empowerment of the Tathāgatas, that your utterance of the circle of sounds and speech may manifest.
Then the Brahmā Bhūteśvara, empowered by the Buddha, looked toward the ten directions with palms joined and spoke thus:

May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, the Great Śrāvakas, and the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas attend to me; may they grant their approval to whoever has this intention:
"May this guidance of the Dharma endure for a long time."
"May there be no harm to the Dharma-preachers and the listeners of the Dharma who are endowed with right practice.
May he grant me this wish so that in the final age, neither Māras, humans, nor non-humans shall cause them harm.
Then that Brahmā Bhūteśvara, for the sake of restraining those of evil intent and for the purpose of taking an oath, let out a loud cry.
And with that sound, he filled this entire world-system.
Furthermore, at that time, all the lords of the Brahmās spoke with one voice, saying:
"We grant our aspiration for this dhāraṇī."

And we ourselves, in the future time, shall uphold this dhāraṇī, we shall proclaim it, we shall protect the true Dharma, and we shall protect those Dharma-preachers and listeners of the Dharma who are endowed with correct practice. Speak, O noble man!
"In the presence of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as well as the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, and the great Śrāvakas, we offer our resolve for this dhāraṇī.
Then, indeed, the Brahmā Bhūteśvara spoke thus:
May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and the Great Śrāvakas empower me! Namely:
Amale, Vimale, Gaṇaṣaṇḍe, Mahāre, Caṇḍe, Mahācaṇḍe!
Came mahācame / some sthāme / avaha vivaha /
O Aṅganī, O destroyer of eyes, O root-severer! O fierce Yakṣa, O fierce Piśāca! O Āvartanī, Saṃvartanī, Saṃkāraṇī, Jambhanī, Mohanī, Uccāṭanī!
hamaha maha maha maha / ākuñcane khagaśava / amale amūla parivarte asārakhava svāhā /
He who would transgress these mantras and not conduct himself in the presence of the assembly—
his eyes will be sealed, his head will burst, and even the disintegration of his limbs will occur.
It is as follows: *acaca avaha / cacacu krakṣa cacaṭa cacāna / khaga caca cacacaca na ca*.

*Amūla-caca amūla-cacaha māmūla-cacaha mūla-mūpaḍa mahā-svāhā!* Then, at that very moment, all the lords of the Brahmās down to the lords of the Piśācas gave their approval, saying: "Excellent! And they spoke thus:
These mantra-words utterly crush the force and power of even a great thousandfold world-system.
This noose is fastened upon all beings who seek to cause harm; how then can they possess life? Brahmā, the Lord of Beings, spoke thus.
Those who possess evil dispositions, who are merciless and ungrateful, beings who desire to harm living creatures, or those belonging to the retinue of Māra who seek an opportunity [to cause harm]—
should they approach Kṣatriya kings, consecrated upon their heads, who have faith in the Buddha’s teaching, seeking an opportunity [to harm them];
or [should they approach] the chief queens, sons, daughters, women of the inner apartments, ministers, soldiers, the military commanders, the courtiers, or others...

Or, those seeking an opportunity to gain entry might approach women, men, boys, girls, laymen (upāsaka), laywomen (upāsikā), Dharma-preachers, listeners of the Dharma, monks (bhikṣu), or nuns (bhikṣuṇī) who are devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, or who are intent upon meditation, recitation, or administrative service.
If they should, even for a single moment, harm, injure, or destroy even a single pore of a sentient being;

or if they should steal their vitality, or discharge breath upon their bodies, or look upon them with a malicious mind— even those Māras, humans, and non-humans whose bodies are moist and foul-smelling— their heads shall split into seven pieces and their eyes shall turn inside out.
Their hearts would wither away; they would become leprous, their bodies moist and foul-smelling, and deprived of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), the earth would open up to receive them,
and winds would scatter them in the four directions.
Covered in dust, those whose minds are distracted shall wander right there;

those who move upon the earth shall enter a fissure in the ground eighty-four thousand *yojanas* deep, and there their lives will come to an end. Those malevolent spirits who move in the water and have no faith in the Buddha’s teaching [shall perish] for the sake of the Kṣatriya kings who are devoted to the Buddha’s teaching.
As for those who would cause harm to the monks engaged in service, their heads shall likewise split into seven pieces;
and for those who should transgress these mantras, their life-span shall end right there and then.
Moreover, in whatever [place]... (Dutt 126)

In whatever region this Dharma discourse of the *Māramaṇḍalāparājita-dhāraṇī* shall circulate, there we shall apply ourselves with zeal for the sake of protection, defense, and guardianship, and we shall fully sustain all those beings there who desire the Dharma. START Rkp 10 (Dutt 127): The Tenth Chapter.
The entire water element, the entire fire element, the entire wind element, and the entire space element were empowered for the sake of the long endurance of the guidance of the True Dharma,

for the sake of the non-interruption of the lineage of the Three Jewels, for the sake of the ripening of all sentient beings, and even for the sake of reaching the further shore of saṃsāra. Then indeed, all those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who dwell in that Buddha-field...

Śakra, Brahmā, and the world-protectors; the lords of the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; and those beings of great majesty and great power, as well as all the resident inhabitants of this world-system of four continents—having addressed them all, he said:
"Friends, for the sake of maturing all sentient beings, I entrust and commit this guidance of the True Dharma into your hands in the greatest measure."
In this way, you must attend to this guide of the True Dharma, kindle it, and protect it,
so that this True Dharma here may not quickly perish or disappear.
And those faithful sons of good family and daughters of good family who shall uphold this Dharma discourse of the Great Collection—

Having written this down, we entrust it into your hands as a deposit for the sake of protecting all those individuals—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—who uphold the True Dharma, so that they may be guarded and sustained.
O preachers of the Dharma! (Dutt 128)
Those persons who desire the Dharma, who delight in meditation, who listen to the Dharma, and who uphold the True Dharma must be protected by you.
Why is that?
Because all those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who have appeared here in this defiled world of the five corruptions—by all those Tathāgatas [they are to be protected].

Having assembled in the Buddha-field, this guidance of the Dharma was entrusted into the hands of all the Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors for their protection, and so forth, until the full maturation of all sentient beings.
In exactly the same way, all those Blessed Buddhas who will appear in the future in the ten directions [will likewise entrust it].

Gathering instantaneously in Buddha-fields afflicted by the five corruptions, they shall speak these words of the dhāraṇī-mantra for the sake of the welfare of sentient beings. They shall empower this guidance of the Dharma and entrust this guidance of the Dharma into the hands of all the Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors for the purpose of guarding and protecting it.

We, too, now entrust this [teaching] extensively into the hands of you who dwell here in our buddha-field— namely, the inhabitants of the four continents, as well as the Śakras, Brahmās, World-Protectors, and the lords of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas—
for the sake of its protection and for the maturation of sentient beings. Therefore,
you must attend to this guide of the True Dharma and cause it to blaze forth, so that it may not quickly fall into ruin or disappear.

Furthermore, those faithful sons of noble family and daughters of noble family, and those individuals who uphold the true Dharma—whether they be monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen—who maintain this Dharma discourse of the Great Assembly, even by having it committed to writing and preserving it;
those Dharma-preachers and listeners of the Dharma who are devoted to meditation and uphold the true Dharma: you must protect them and honor them.
For what reason?
This Dharma-discourse is sustained by the empowerment of all the Buddhas;
wherever it may be—in a village, a city, a town, a district, a market-town, a royal court, or a forest hermitage—[it shall prevail].

Or wherever this Dharma-discourse may circulate, be proclaimed, taught, or mastered— even if only by being written in a book and recited— in that household or in a village, through that essence of the Dharma, the vitality of the earth and the vigor of sentient beings will increase.
By means of that, you shall become possessed of vigor, and endowed with brilliance, strength, heroism, and prowess.
Your retinues and celestial palaces shall increase; even the kings of men will become your protectors. Through royal sovereignty you shall prosper, and your entire kingdom shall be well-guarded.
And by that flavor of the Dharma, the kings in Jambudvīpa will be thoroughly satisfied; they will possess minds intent on mutual benefit,
they will have faith in the ripening of karma,
and they will be virtuous in mind.
The kings will be free from envy, intent on beneficial matters, possessed of compassion for all sentient beings, and even endowed with right view;
they will each take delight in their own respective territories,
and this Jambudvīpa will become prosperous, magnificent, and densely populated.
It will become more abundant in food and more delightful;
the earth will be crowded with many people and endowed with vitality, becoming more lush, and its fruits will be softer.
Therein, it shall become exceedingly abundant with medicinal herbs, wealth, and grain, and shall produce health, happiness, and pleasant dwellings.

All strife, quarrels, famine, disease, foreign invasions, gadflies, mosquitoes, locusts, venomous serpents, wicked yakṣas, rākṣasas, wild beasts, birds, and wolves, as well as untimely winds and rains, shall be pacified.
The constellations, nights, days, fortnights, seasons, and years shall proceed correctly.
They will cause [the Dharma] to flow forth;
and for the most part, sentient beings will practice the ten paths of wholesome action.
Having passed away from here, they will go to happy destinies and the celestial realms.
They, too, shall become your retinue.

Thus, this Dharma discourse of the dhāraṇī, the Great Assembly empowered by all Buddhas, possesses many virtues and great benefits; it will serve for the crossing to the further shore of the conditioned formations of sentient beings and for the increase and fulfillment of their glory.

For the sake of the complete exhaustion of the female state without remainder— whether that karma is to be experienced upon rebirth, in a subsequent life, or briefly even in the present life— that entire projected female selfhood will go to total destruction,
with the exception of one who has committed an act of immediate retribution, or one who rejects the True Dharma, or one who slanders the Noble Ones.
Whatever other depravity there may be regarding the ripening of the fruits of body, speech, and mind, all that will go to complete exhaustion.

For one who, at the very least, preserves this Dharma-discourse even by having it written in a book, their obstructions of karma and afflictions as vast as Mount Sumeru will go to complete exhaustion,
and all objects of their roots of virtue will reach growth and fulfillment.
There will be the fulfillment of all limbs, the accomplishment of all intentions, and the increase of all good conduct of body, speech, and mind.
There will be the abandonment of all wrong views, the subjugation of all enemies in accordance with the Dharma, and the entry into the subtle and peaceful path.

By the power of this *Mahāsaṃnipāta-dhāraṇī* discourse on the Dharma, which is sustained by the empowerment of all Buddhas, in whatever region this discourse on the Dharma shall again circulate, there—
The earth will become more moist; it will be full of vitality, with soft fruits and sweet juices,
and it will be entirely free from bitter, pungent, harsh, and tasteless things.

There will be an abundance of flowers and fruits; there will be an increase in wealth, grain, treasuries, granaries, jars, and vases; and clothing, food, drink, medicine, and utensils will become most plentiful.

Furthermore, those beings there who subsist on food and drink will become healthier, more beautiful, strong, mindful, wise, and devoted to the Dharma; they will delight in seeking what is wholesome and be entirely free from evil.
Having passed away from there, they will be reborn as your companions.
Thus, with your retinues increased, powerful, and possessing unimpeded wheels, you shall protect the fourfold community of people through the power of the Dharma;
you shall establish sentient beings in the purposes of the Dharma.
"In this way, you will have performed worship for all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who follow throughout the three times.

Then, the Tathāgata Māndāravagandharoca, filling this entire buddha-field with a pure sound of speech that accorded with the expression of meaningful words through his Buddha-range knowledge and voice, addressed all the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, Śakras, Indras, and so forth...
The lords of Brahmā, the lords of Indra, and the lords of the great nāgas— those who dwell here in this buddha-field, and especially those who dwell in this four-continent world-system—
were, by the word of all the Blessed Buddhas, exhorted to uphold, proclaim, and protect the eye of the Dharma of this *Saṃnipāta-sūtra*.
Furthermore, at that time, ninety-seven thousand koṭis of great beings who had attained patient acceptance (*kṣānti*), led by Maitreya and residing in this buddha-field,
all spoke with one voice as follows:
"We too, by the word of all the Blessed Buddhas and the Tathāgatas who have followed throughout the three times..."

For the sake of worship, we shall receive this Dharma-discourse according to principle and as approved by the treatises, with reverence for our teacher. Out of compassion, for the sake of maturing sentient beings and for the sake of establishing them on the unsurpassed path, we shall extensively illuminate this Dharma-discourse in villages, towns, market towns, districts, royal capitals, and forest hermitages.
"And we shall bring sentient beings to maturity for the sake of the long endurance of the True Dharma.
Then, at that time, all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who were within those Buddha-fields, gave their approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O noble sons! It is exactly as you should do."

Then indeed, all the Śakras, Brahmās, and lords of the Mahoragas, as well as another sixty-four *koṭī-nayuta* of beings of great and immense power in this Buddha-field, all spoke with one voice: "We too shall take up this Dharma-discourse of the Great Assembly;
we shall proclaim it extensively, illuminate it, and bring sentient beings to maturity, so that the True Dharma may endure for a long time."
We shall protect and preserve those who uphold the true Dharma and those who listen to the Dharma.

And wherever this Dharma-discourse shall circulate, there, by the word of all the Blessed Buddhas, we shall pacify all strife, quarrels, conflicts, disputes, famines, diseases, foreign armies, untimely winds, rains, cold, and heat, as well as all wicked, harsh, rough, tasteless, bitter, and pungent conditions.

We shall bring about security, delightfulness, and an abundance of all necessities; we shall apply ourselves with effort for the sake of the long endurance of the guidance of the True Dharma; and we shall, to a greater degree, protect righteous kings.
"And we shall protect those beings who delight in meditative concentration.
Then all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, gave their approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O gentle-faced ones!"
Thus you must act;
you should apply yourselves with diligence for the sake of yourself, others, and both.
And in this way, you will have performed worship to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who belong to the three times.

Since you are indeed thus exerted for the sake of maturing sentient beings, for the sake of kindling the eye of the true Dharma, and for the sake of the long endurance of the true Dharma, before long you shall swiftly and fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Then,

all those who dwell in this central four-continent world system— the Śakras, Brahmās, lords of the gods, lords of the mahoragas, and those beings of great power and great majesty— rose from their seats.
Standing with palms joined in reverence, they spoke thus:
"We too, by the word of all the Blessed Buddhas, shall illuminate and protect this guidance of the True Dharma;
and we shall duly receive this *Mahāsannipāta*, the Dharma-discourse on the *dhāraṇī* and *mudrā* empowered by all the Buddhas."

We shall extensively proclaim [this] throughout villages, towns, market towns, districts, royal capitals, and forest hermitages; and we shall protect and preserve those individuals who uphold the True Dharma—
those Dharma-preachers established in the practice of the Dharma, as well as the listeners of the Dharma, including monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.

We shall protect, preserve, honor, revere, and worship all those faithful sons of good family and daughters of good family who will take up this Dharma-discourse, and even those who, devoted to meditation, shall uphold it by having it written down in a book, providing them with robes, parasols, banners, flags, ointments, and so forth.
We shall honor them with all medicinal requisites;
and while this Dharma-discourse is being spoken and elucidated, we ourselves will approach to hear it, regarding it with the same perception as that of the Teacher.
We shall honor, revere, respect, and worship this Dharma-discourse with parasols, banners, and flags.
For what reason?
Because when this Dharma discourse on the dhāraṇī-seal, empowered by all the Buddhas, is being proclaimed, we shall become endowed with vitality through the essence of the Dharma;
we shall become strong, heroic, mindful, wise, possessed of a retinue of followers, and endowed with the prowess of an unimpeded wheel.

In this way, we shall pacify all conditions in every realm that bring about strife, quarrels, disputes, famine, disease, foreign invasions, untimely winds, rain, excessive cold and heat, drought, bad dreams, ill omens, and all unwholesome factors such as foul, harsh, rough, bitter, pungent,
and tasteless things; and to a greater degree, we shall bring about a state of security, abundance, delight, health, and harmony.
We shall, in due time, summon the winds, rains, cold, heat, and floods;
we shall correctly summon the planets, nights, days, months, fortnights, seasons, and years;
and we shall correctly cause the planets, constellations, sun, and moon to revolve.
We shall fill the rivers, lakes, ponds, and lotus-pools;
wherever there is suffering for sentient beings caused by floods of water, we shall ward that off.

To a greater degree, for the sake of the welfare of beings in those villages, towns, market-towns, and provinces, we shall [provide] leaves, branches, flowers, fruits, fragrances, grains, medicinal herbs, and crops that are glossy, polished, excellent in color and taste, and exceedingly abundant.
We shall bring them to fulfillment;
we shall provide for beings so that they lack nothing by means of wealth, grain, medicinal herbs, clothing, and ornaments.
And for those beings, through their pursuit of the wholesome, the Dharma-discourse known as the *Dhāraṇīmudrā* shall be revealed.
Even if it is merely written in a book, we shall preserve it or recite it, or preserve it with honor and reverence;
and as for those who will be kings among them— those consecrated Kṣatriyas— we shall protect and sustain them.
We shall remove what is harmful for them,
and we shall bring about what is beneficial for them.
We shall pacify all forms of curiosity, auspicious rites, wrong views, evil deeds, false empowerments, evil vows, evil refuges, hypocrisy, chatter, deceit, guile, lying, envy, and anger.
We shall establish them upon the straight path of right view—in faith, self-restraint, self-control, moral shame, and dread of blame.

In this same way, we shall provide protection and guardianship for the chief queens, the women of the inner apartments, the assembly of ministers, the high officials, the merchants, the citizens, and the people of the countryside; and for those of the four castes—women, men, boys, and girls—we shall likewise establish them in moral shame and dread of blame.
We shall protect even the four-footed animals within those regions;
we shall ensure the proclamation of this Dharma-discourse wherever it remains, even when merely written in a book.
With such great efforts and valor, we shall nurture those beings for the sake of illuminating the guidance of the Dharma and shall apply ourselves to its preservation so that it does not disappear.
Then all those Blessed Buddhas gave their approval to those noble beings, saying:

"Excellent, excellent, O gentle-faced ones! It is right that you should act in this way, since you are dedicated to ensuring that the guidance of the Dharma and the lineage of the Three Jewels do not perish; in this manner, [you honor] the Buddhas who follow throughout all three times."
"An offering will have been made to the Blessed Ones.
Thus ends the tenth chapter, "On Protection," in the *Ratnaketu Sūtra*.
START Rkp 11 (Dutt 136): The Eleventh Chapter.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, addressed Śakra, Brahmā, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Kuvera: "O gentle-faced ones, through the vow of compassion for sentient beings in this defiled Buddha-field of the five corruptions, I have awakened to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment for the sake of those beings who are cast into the darkness of ignorance and harassed by the thieves and rogues of the afflictions."

For the sake of pacifying the afflictions, the faction of Māra has been defeated by me; the banner of the True Dharma has been raised high; immeasurable sentient beings have been liberated from suffering;
the rain of the True Dharma has been released; and tens of millions of Māras have been defeated by me.

O noble ones, that which I now entrust into your hands is this Dharma discourse— the *Vajradharmasamatā-pratītyadharmahṛdaya-sarvasamucchraya-vidhvaṃsana-dhāraṇīmudrāpadaprabhedapraveśavyākaraṇa*— which has been empowered and protected by these immeasurable, incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas assembled from the world-systems of the ten directions.

"In this Buddha-field, for the sake of pacifying the defects of the earth's essence and the dwelling places of sentient beings, for the sake of maturing sentient beings, for the sake of the complete exhaustion of all unwholesome karma without remainder, for the sake of the long endurance of the lineage of the Three Jewels, and for the sake of fulfilling the intentions of the Buddhas— you also must, through your empowerment, protect this. Furthermore, whatever accumulations of roots of merit and merit there are from my preservation of the guide of the True Dharma, and whatever accumulations of roots of merit and merit there are from reciting, teaching, remembering, and reading [this], from going for refuge to the Triple Gem, from the upāsaka vows, and from abiding in the celibate life (*brahmacarya*)."

[From the cultivation of the first dhyāna] up to the cultivation of the cessation of perception and feeling; from the realization of the fruit of stream-entry up to other formations of roots of merit and merit that have been performed by me now, or are to be performed in the future— namely, these formations of merit consisting in the kindling of the lamp of the True Dharma.
I entrust all of this into your hands. ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...

... ... ... ... ... ... For the sake of proclaiming this Dharma-discourse, we shall encourage the person who is a Dharma-preacher; we shall accomplish the increase of wealth, grain, and all enjoyments for the Dharma-preachers and those who listen to the Dharma.
"We shall uphold the teaching of the Jina, which is of an indestructible nature.
Then all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, gave their approval to all humans and non-humans.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kautūhalika sought out that Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
“Blessed One, have ten million Māras arrived together with their retinues?
The Blessed One replied,
“All of them, together with their retinues.”
Then the Bodhisattva Kautūhalika asked,
"Have the Māras and their retinues gained faith in the Three Jewels?
The Blessed One said:

Noble son, this Māra, the Evil One, accompanied by a retinue of a thousand, having failed to gain faith, is angry and displeased; even as he remains so now, in the future time as well, he will strive to destroy the guidance of the True Dharma, watching for an opportunity and seeking an opening. [In that same way... these twenty-one members of his retinue, having failed to gain faith, are angry and displeased.

Even during the present and future times, as long as the guidance of the True Dharma continues to spread, these individuals will seek an opportunity for entry and search for an opening within my teaching, striving for the purpose of destroying the guidance of the True Dharma.
For what reason?
Because they are possessed by former enmity, because they have not planted roots of merit, because they are under the influence of non-virtuous friends, ...

because they have not attained serene confidence in the bliss of nirvāṇa, and because they are encompassed by [wrong] aspirations, they do not join mind to mind; they do not find serenity, they do not remain settled, and they do not attain composure.
"Having seen the great assembly of the Buddhas and having heard the profound *dhāraṇī*, by this very cause he will later attain faith;
he will obtain serene confidence in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then the Bodhisattva Kautūhalika said:

"Blessed One, if this Dharma-discourse should resound in the ears of even those beings who have not previously planted roots of merit, may they generate the aspiration for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Now at that time, there was a Māra named Nāgadatta who had previously made a vow for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
he [approached] Śākyamuni in the guise of a great ṛṣi."
[The Mahāsannipāta-ratnaketu-dhāraṇī-sūtra is completed.]
